reviews.title: Advertising
reviews.text: This app is truly beautiful and I love using it to get closer to my father but the amount of advertising that is in this app is almost like if you payed to go to church. I mean I can’t take a walk with god without paying. I get ads for a glorify ring. It is equivalent to when Jesus walked into a church and saw markets they were making profit off religion this is wrong and a sin.

reviews.title: Disappointed

reviews.title: Beautiful App💗 but accessibility barrier for dyslexia
reviews.text:
I really love using Glorify - the daily devotionals, prayers, and overall design are wonderful for building a regular routine. However, there is a major accessibility issue that needs to be addressed. As someone with dyslexia, reading large blocks of text is a significant barrier, yet the audio-listening feature is locked behind the paid subscription.

While I understand monetizing premium content, basic audio playback is essential assistive technology for neurodivergent and visually impaired users. Connecting with God shouldn't be harder or more expensive just because of a learning disability. I truly hope the developers consider making basic audio narration free so the app can be accessible to everyone in the community.

reviews.title: Glorify-Lite
reviews.text: This is a great example of ‘theory of inevitable gradualism’. With each update, the product became less than, and the ‘gradual’ drive towards ‘pay us’ for this product! Until the ‘inevitable’ conclusion of what the entire app was created for. Money! If this were not true, why not offer a Family Plan? How many subscriptions in one family will satisfy this now Glorify-Less-pay more? Yes, there is already one paid subscription in this family and was happy with my free version for 785 days in a row. I do know where this began and have sadly watched this happen. Would I pay if it still had the Glorious deep scriptural devotions? In a heartbeat! I will NOT be forced to pay for the level of writing I could write. By the way, the free content compared with the paid subscription, is exactly the same! I have written them after each update, this is not news to them. Each reply is an acknowledgment of what I said and an justification of what they’re doing. I feel they have driven me to a point of bad review by telling me, ‘they will give my suggestion of a family plan to the team.’ And what? Gradually putting me here and inevitably making me pay? For what? Other free Biblical publications start offering MORE if you pay! Not manipulations to pay for LESS! Thank you for making this dishonest decision for me! JC

reviews.title: Disappointing Changes
reviews.text: I’ve used and loved this app for a long time because of its free daily devotional that I’m able to listen to while I get ready for work each morning. But recently they suddenly, without warning, put a subscription charge of £4.99 on it. This is so disappointing. Even more disappointing is that when I commented my disappointment on their instagram page, instead of messaging me about it, they just deleted the comment and ignored me. Such a shame as it was such a great devotional app made available to anyone. But not anymore!

reviews.title: Glorify’s Business Practices
reviews.text:
Glorify started as a wonderful app that seemed to really prioritize the message of God. The call to all believers is to go forth and make disciples, and this app was doing a phenomenal job of building an intentional, daily opportunity to engage with God and grow fellow believers in Christ. However, over the years, they’ve continually drawn back on free features and now there is not much left to do at all unless you are a paid subscriber. The nature of the app itself has now changed, and what should be free for all to experience and learn in Christ is now paywalled. 

I don’t believe that there’s anything wrong with having paid features in an app, but ALL of these features started off as free, it’s astonishing to see they’ve left little unpaid now. I’m very disheartened to say that I will now be uninstalling the app. I do not wish to support a company that has changed to view believers and their faith as business models. An app now only useful for those willing to pay.

reviews.title: It was good until it wasn’t.
reviews.text: I use to love glorify! It was was apart of my daily routine! I either started my day reading Glorify or ended in sauna listening to glorify. I’ve had glorify for about two years but recently had to delete it. Ever since they’ve updated the app what seems like every month, it hasn’t hit my spirit the same. (Example: having to subscribe to listen to the ‘daily walk with God’ really crushed my spirit because that was my favorite meditation session!) Since these updates I don’t feel like Glorify’s mission is to attract people to Gods glory. I feel like they are running a business now rather than an experience. Because of this uneasiness, I’ve deleted glorify after not only using it daily but recommending it to a good handful of my close friends. Since deleting this app it has been very hard to find a meditation experience that talks to you about the goodness of God & whose mission is to attract all people to understand his goodness. This devastates me but I must listen to my spirit when it comes to others motives of using Gods word.
